justification: Deletes an invented default lot frontage from a LIVE surface: app/assessment/page.tsx:563 mounts StateLevelControls, which mounts HousingSEPPEligibilityCard. Unlike PR #1230, a user could see this. Not Critical: the figure fed an eligibility display, not a write, a migration or a served regulatory quote, and the fix is predominantly deletion of a constant that was defeating a guard the component already had. Not Minor: it changes which housing types a property is shown as eligible for, narrows a component prop from number to number|null, and changes when the whole LMR section renders.

pre_impl.existing_data: HousingSEPPEligibilityCard already handled a missing frontage correctly: its useEffect skips the eligibility fetch on a falsy lotWidth and the component renders a card asking for lot size and frontage width. It also already carries an assessmentStatus of not_assessed, added earlier for exactly this shape of problem. The default of 15 metres meant those guards never ran, so the fix is mostly deletion rather than new logic.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I reported to the user that the page printed Frontage 15.0m in the amber panel. Reading the code showed that was wrong: the amber panel renders only when lmrFrontageStatus returns a non-empty excluded list, and a 15 clears all three minimums, so that panel returned null and printed nothing at all. The real harm there is suppression of the caveat, not a wrong number. The wrong number was printed by the eligibility card instead, at a different line. Both are now covered, and the mutation harness separately disproved a third assumption of mine by showing one display line is unreachable.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One constant deleted, one prop widened to nullable, one explanatory note added, and the frontage resolution moved out of the 1,600-line component into lib/geometry/effective-lot-width.ts, which already owned battleaxeAwareLotWidth, so it became unit-testable rather than only source-asserted. positiveFiniteOrNull is applied inside battleaxeAwareLotWidth and battleaxeAwareLotDepth as well, so a 0 or NaN can no longer escape those functions, win a caller's chain and only then be rejected. The LMR section gate was changed from isLMRArea && lotSize && lotWidth to isLMRArea && lotSize: keeping lotWidth would have newly hidden the whole section for every property whose frontage is unknown, because the invented 15 had made that condition always true.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/components/compliance/no-invented-lot-width.test.tsx lib/geometry/__tests__/effective-lot-width.test.ts && npx tsc --noEmit && python C:/Users/lawre/.claude/jobs/725925e0/tmp/mutate_width.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The suites go red if the constant returns to the shipped NSW_PLANNING_CONSTANTS object under its own name or a renamed one, if any width is substituted anywhere in the candidate list, if the LMR section is gated on lotWidth again, if the not-checked note is removed, if the eligibility fetch runs without a frontage, if a 0, NaN, Infinity or negative is accepted as a measurement, or if candidates are coalesced before being normalised rather than after.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 20 of 20 component tests and 44 of 44 geometry tests pass on clean code; npx tsc --noEmit exits 0; the full frontend suite is 119 suites and 1736 tests with 0 failures. The evidence is the mutation harness: 10 mutations applied one at a time and reverted byte-for-byte, 10 of 10 CAUGHT, 0 holes. It found three real holes on the way, none of which review had spotted. First, asserting the bare name of the normaliser passed even after its call was replaced by an inline passthrough, because the function's own definition matched. Second, leaving a 15 fallback inside the normaliser call reinstated the original defect exactly, since 15 is positive and finite, while every other assertion still passed. Third, a candidate list is now asserted to contain no nullish operator at all, because one there cannot normalise the values it chooses between. An eleventh candidate is UNCATCHABLE and is recorded as such in both the harness and the suite rather than being dropped.

functions.name: lmrFrontageStatus
functions.input: A frontage in metres, now only ever a figure taken from cadastral geometry rather than a substituted default, because the caller guards on null before calling it.
functions.output: Two lists, excluded and eligible, built by comparing that frontage against the three LMR minimums of 12, 12 and 15 metres.
functions.if_none: Unchanged and still takes a plain number; the null case is handled by the caller, which renders an explicit not-checked note instead of calling this at all.

functions.name: StateLevelControls lotWidth resolution
functions.input: The battleaxe-aware cadastral width, then the geometry frontage, then the estimated width, then the constraints width, each tried in order.
functions.output: A measured frontage in metres when any source holds one, typed explicitly as number or null so the compiler keeps the nullability.
functions.if_none: Null. It used to be 15, which cleared every LMR minimum; now the component states that the frontage minimums have not been checked.

functions.name: HousingSEPPEligibilityCard
functions.input: zoneCode, lotSize and lotWidth, with lotWidth now typed as number or null to match what the caller can actually supply.
functions.output: The eligibility list fetched from the housing-sepp route, together with a property summary line that prints the frontage it was given.
functions.if_none: Skips the fetch entirely and renders a card saying lot size and frontage width are needed, which is the guard the deleted constant had been defeating.

functions.name: firstMeasuredWidth
functions.input: The frontage candidates in preference order, each of which may be a number, null or undefined, and any of which may be an upstream sentinel.
functions.output: The first candidate that is a positive finite number, normalised before the comparison rather than after it, so an invalid earlier candidate cannot shadow a valid later one.
functions.if_none: Null when no candidate is a measurement, which the caller renders as an explicit statement that the frontage minimums were not checked.

functions.name: positiveFiniteOrNull
functions.input: An unknown value from cadastral geometry, a planning constraint or a parseFloat that may have failed.
functions.output: That value when it is a positive finite number, which is the only shape that counts as a measured frontage or depth.
functions.if_none: Null for 0, negative zero, a negative, NaN, Infinity, a numeric string, null, undefined or an object, each asserted in the geometry suite.

values: N/A -- no value is read from a database or an API by this change. The figure removed was a literal constant in source, and the figures it was compared against are the LMR minimums already held in lib/see/propertyUtils.ts.

break_it.what_happens: firstMeasuredWidth normalises each candidate before comparing, so NaN followed by 13 returns 13. Two mutations cover it: coalescing first and normalising afterwards, and putting a nullish operator back into the component's candidate list.
break_it.how: The resolution moved out of the 1,600-line component into lib/geometry/effective-lot-width.ts so it is unit-testable, and the component's candidate list is asserted to contain no nullish operator.

verdicts.finding: MEDIUM null-guard, StateLevelControls.tsx:1029 (round 1) -- the missing-frontage notice checks only for null while the adjacent eligibility logic treats every falsy width as missing, so a 0 or NaN sentinel is handled inconsistently and partially silently.
verdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED and FIXED. The nullish operator falls through only on null and undefined, so an upstream 0 sentinel or a failed parseFloat survived the chain, and the result was worse than inconsistent, it was silent: the null check was false so the new not-checked notice was hidden, and the truthiness check was false so the amber panel was hidden too, leaving no frontage text anywhere beside a card separately asking for one.

verdicts.finding: MEDIUM correctness, StateLevelControls.tsx:517 (round 2) -- normalising only after the nullish chain lets an invalid earlier candidate such as 0, NaN, Infinity or a negative prevent a later valid frontage from being used.
verdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED and FIXED, and it was a defect in my own round-1 fix rather than in the original code. battleaxeAwareLotWidth could return NaN, because its final check was a typeof test and typeof NaN is number; that NaN then won the chain and my trailing normaliser turned it into null, discarding a valid 13 metre frontage sitting in the next candidate. I had traded a false number for a false unavailable, which is quieter and still wrong. Each candidate is now normalised before the comparison, the resolver lives in the geometry module where it can be unit-tested, and the behaviour is asserted directly rather than through the component's source.
